summary.business: Divgi TorqTransfer Systems designs and manufactures system-level driveline solutions for the automotive components space, including transfer cases, torque couplers and dual-clutch transmissions (DCTs), supported by in-house software capabilities. It supplies electronically controlled driveline systems to leading OEMs including Tata Motors and Mahindra & Mahindra, and has developed multiple EV transmission products in-house, including India's first indigenously mass-produced EV transmissions. The Company operates four manufacturing facilities and sells both into the Indian OEM base and, increasingly, into export drivetrain programmes.

Components and software: 32-bit processor developed for BorgWarner transfer case applications

currentContext.expansion: The Company describes FY 2025-26 as a year of expansion in its export business rather than of new plant construction: it secured exclusive transfer case supply opportunities supporting overseas vehicle programmes, including export-linked programmes for international markets, winning them against established international suppliers. Management expects exports to become a significant contributor to long-term growth as recently secured programmes move towards higher volumes and the opportunity pipeline strengthens. On the domestic side, stronger demand from key OEM customers translated into higher volumes and improved capacity utilisation, with greater participation in premium utility vehicle platforms raising content per vehicle. Growth came largely from the existing asset base - the AR states that much of the revenue growth was achieved without a proportionate increase in capital expenditure, demonstrating the scalability of the manufacturing infrastructure, and that capacity remains adequately utilised with substantial headroom to support future growth as electric mobility programmes gain scale. FY 2025-26 capital allocation was directed towards technology development, manufacturing capability enhancement and product engineering initiatives, intended to deepen participation in higher-value drivetrain applications, support EV and advanced transmission opportunities, enhance localisation and strengthen customer engagement across domestic and international markets - funded largely through internal accruals from a virtually debt-free, net-cash balance sheet. Environment- and safety-linked investments named in the BRSR include installation of a fire hydrant, rooftop solar, rainwater harvesting and a safety DOJO. No named plant, line or commissioning timeline is disclosed in this bundle.

risks.risk: Concentration on a niche driveline segment
risks.note: Management flags that a shift in consumer demand could hurt the Company given its concentrated focus on a specific niche segment; the stated mitigation is diversifying the portfolio across passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles, tractors and construction equipment, and across more customer segments and geographies.

risks.risk: Cyclicality of automobile demand / economic slowdown
risks.note: An economic slowdown could adversely impact performance because reduced automobile demand translates directly into lower revenues. Mitigation cited is a footprint expanded across four countries and diversified product applications to limit dependence on a narrow set of markets.

risks.risk: Intense global competition on cost and scale
risks.note: Competitive pressure is driven by cost efficiency and scale of production, where global Tier-1 peers have far larger volumes; the Company relies on lean-manufacturing-driven cost optimisation to defend its position.

risks.risk: Technology obsolescence in a drivetrain transition
risks.note: Management explicitly flags that innovations may render existing technologies obsolete - a live risk for a transfer-case and transmission maker as the industry shifts to electrification, requiring consistent investment in technological upgrades.

risks.risk: OEM ESG and carbon-footprint screening of suppliers
risks.note: Global OEMs increasingly require carbon footprint evaluation and life cycle assessments of supplier products, tightening screening and selection criteria; failure to qualify would close off programme awards. The Company cites multi-year ISO 14000 certification and use of the GRI framework as its response.

risks.risk: OEM cost-down pressure alongside rising quality demands
risks.note: Global OEMs are placing greater emphasis on reducing costs while simultaneously improving quality, compressing supplier margins; the Company responds with a CMM-based vendor development programme, a supplier quality improvement initiative and complementary capital equipment.

Long-term success and sustainability are said to be at risk if the Company cannot attract and retain skilled talent - relevant for an engineering- and software-intensive business; the MD&A reports 278 employees as on 31 March 2026 and a retention rate of over 13.07%.

risks.risk: Climate / GHG exposure and tightening environmental regulation
risks.note: The BRSR material-issues table identifies climate protection as a risk with negative financial implications, since manufacturing GHG emissions and energy-intensive machinery, heating, cooling and lighting are core to operations; separately, management flags that stricter environmental regulations could challenge the growth trajectory.

risks.risk: Regulatory compliance and governance process lapses
risks.note: The BRSR flags regulatory compliance as a risk-and-opportunity where non-compliance can lead to fines, legal penalties and litigation. The Secretarial Auditor reported two observations for the year: a gap of more than 210 days between two Risk Management Committee meetings (attributed to administrative oversight), and the Chairman of the Stakeholders Relationship Committee not being present at the AGM held during FY 2025-2026.

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Indian wholesale vehicle volume growth is expected to normalise to a moderate 3-6% across segments in FY 2026-27, following a high-growth phase in the latter half of FY 2025-26 driven by post-GST factors and strong rural demand.
- Passenger vehicle volumes are projected to grow 4-6% YoY in FY 2026-27 (5-7% in FY 2025-26 before moderating, amid elevated inventories); two-wheelers 3-5% on a higher base; commercial vehicles 4-6%, with buses growing faster at 7-9% on replacement cycles.
- Utility vehicles continue to outperform and the share of alternative powertrains - CNG, hybrids and EVs - is steadily increasing, shifting the mix toward higher-technology content.
- The Indian auto component industry is undergoing a structural shift driven by electrification, tighter safety norms and rapid digital integration, evolving from mechanical manufacturing into a hub for advanced electronic and technology-led components.
- Increasing technological complexity is fostering deeper collaboration between Tier-1 suppliers and OEMs on integrated solutions, creating opportunities in power electronics, battery management systems and ADAS.
- Global supply chain volatility - especially semiconductor shortages - remains a key challenge, with companies responding through localisation and digital supply chain strategies.
- India's auto components market is projected to grow by USD 85.85 billion between 2025 and 2030, a 14.8% CAGR over the forecast period.
- The Indian EV transition is a stated growth driver: passenger EV sales exceeded 199,000 units in FY 2025-26 (over 80% YoY growth) and EVs were approximately 7% of total sales in Q3 FY 2025-26, with the India Automotive Mission Plan 2047 targeting a 30% EV share of new vehicle sales by 2030.
- The global automotive market is projected to expand from USD 4,543.97 billion in 2025 to USD 7,458.15 billion by 2034 (5.66% CAGR), while the global auto parts market grows from USD 2,302.2 billion in 2025 to USD 2,818.9 billion by 2034 (2.21% CAGR over 2026-2034).
- Competitive differentiation across the industry is shifting from price-based competition to innovation, technology and supply chain resilience.
- Macro backdrop: the World Bank has revised its FY 2026-27 India growth estimate upward to approximately 6.6%, supported by resilient private consumption, low inflation, GST rationalisation and Union Budget tax relief, with risks from elevated energy prices and uncertain global demand.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Leadership position in India's automotive transmission solutions space, with system-level (not component-level) offerings
- Pioneered India's first indigenously mass-produced EV transmissions and developed multiple EV transmission products in-house
- Commissioned India's first high-speed dynamometer for manual transmission, EV transmission and 4WD transfer case applications
- In-house software, mechatronics and systems-integration capability alongside advanced manufacturing
- Long-standing relationships with leading OEMs including Tata Motors and Mahindra & Mahindra
- Value-engineering track record with global customers - developed a cost-effective 32-bit processor for BorgWarner, replacing legacy 8-bit technology in transfer case applications
- Cost optimisation through lean manufacturing practices, cited by management as a competitive differentiator
- Intellectual capital base of 6 registered IPRs and FY 2025-26 R&D spend of Rs 11.79 crore
- Flexible delivery models including overseas safety stock in the United States and Mexico to de-risk customer supply chains

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Indonesia order] Secured an exclusive order as sole supplier from a key OEM customer for 4x4 transfer cases for the Indonesian Pik-Up program, with production expected from CY26; the Indonesia 4x4 ramp-up is named as the primary growth driver, with incremental volumes expected through the remaining quarters of FY27.
- [Export approvals] Received final production approval on all export parts with additional revenue potential of ~Rs. 10 to 12 crores per month; FY27 component exports are targeted at ~Rs. 80 crore.
- [Export trajectory] Exports revenue of Rs. 13.55 Cr (FY23), Rs. 3.42 Cr (FY24), Rs. 10.80 Cr (FY25) and Rs. 66.90 Cr (FY26), with the FY26 exports share shown at 18% of total revenue; geographic mix in the latest quarter shown as 84% Domestic / 16% Exports.
- [Partnership channel] Exclusive distribution agreement with Toyota Tsusho for Divgi-TTS products to Japanese companies worldwide, opening Japan, South Korea, Thailand, Indonesia and China; new AWD and PTU programmes cited as further diversification avenues.
- [Ownership history] Journey slide records the BorgWarner JV, BorgWarner's exit via buy-out of shares, investments by NRJN Family Trust and Oman India Joint Investment Fund II, and the 2020 amalgamation into Divgi TorqTransfer Systems.
